title: HIV Clinical Fellowship
purpose: As the HIV epidemic and workforce evolve, there is a critical need for physicians trained in comprehensive HIV care who can lead, innovate, and serve diverse communities.

program.description: A two-year postdoctoral fellowship that trains primary care physicians in advanced HIV care, research, and teaching. We seek candidates who are:
qualifiedPhysicians: Committed to delivering comprehensive HIV care and prevention, especially for vulnerable communities
Dedicated to leadership in healthcare, education, and advocacy
Interested in healthcare systems, research, and policy

history: Founded in 2001, the HIV Clinical Fellowship (HCF) was among the first U.S. programs dedicated to HIV care. Based at a leading Los Angeles clinic, it was developed by the Los Angeles AETC at the Keck School of Medicine of USC, Department of Family Medicine.
In 2016, HCF partnered with Los Angeles County Department of Health Services (DHS)—the nation’s second-largest municipal safety-net system—expanding its reach and impact.
description: A two-year fellowship for physicians in Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, or Med-Peds dedicated to advancing HIV primary and specialty care for underserved populations, including those experiencing homelessness, substance use, incarceration, and underinsurance.
Over 30 fellows have graduated to date, many now serving in leadership and clinical roles across community health centers, academia, and public health.
